amends: M9.7 (does not alter M9.6 or M9.7's own historical artifacts, per Section 1 rule 9 'Historical artifacts/checkpoints/results are immutable' -- every M9.7 report file listed in m9_7_artifacts_hash_snapshot below is byte-identical to its state at M9.7 closure; this amendment is additive only)
purpose: Fix a checkpoint-selection inconsistency in the M9.8 design M9.7 froze, discovered BEFORE any M9.8 execution and BEFORE any HydroCore-M development/predictive performance was observed. Does not reopen, re-tune, or re-derive any other M9.7-frozen quantity.

problem_identified.statement: m9-7-training-parity-plan.json's checkpoint_selection.policy field reads 'validation only (lowest validation loss across the run, per-family mean for interleaved training)', with no mention of M9.6's own promotion-authoritative canonical checkpoint. m9-7-m9-8-preregistration.json's ARM_S definition says to reuse 'M9.6's own trained checkpoints' without specifying WHICH of M9.6's two recorded checkpoints per seed (best-validation vs. canonical FINAL_STEP_1350) that means. M9.6 itself did NOT use best-validation as its promotion-authoritative checkpoint: m9_6_common.CANONICAL_CHECKPOINT_POLICY = 'FINAL_STEP_1350', both run_m9_6_train_arm_a.py and run_m9_6_train_arm_b.py export a SEPARATE canonical FINAL_STEP_1350 checkpoint after training completes (Section 14 of both scripts), and run_m9_6_evaluate.py's _canonical_model helper loads record['canonical_export_path'] (the FINAL_STEP_1350 export) -- NOT record['best_validation_export_path'] -- for every number M9.6's own M9_6_DECISION=A rested on. Left as originally worded, a future M9.8 executor could legally satisfy M9.7's own text by checkpointing ARM_M (freshly trained) at best-validation while ARM_S (reused from M9.6) is actually the FINAL_STEP_1350 canonical checkpoint -- a checkpoint-selection-criterion mismatch between the two arms being compared, which would break the intended exact-compute capacity comparison even though the OPTIMIZER-STEP budget (1350/1350) was already correctly matched.
problem_identified.concrete_evidence_of_real_divergence_ris: Not merely theoretical: reports/evaluation/hydrocore-v5/m9-6/m9-6-training-runs/ARM_B_M9_6-seed20260814.json (an already-committed, immutable M9.6 artifact) records best_epoch=12 while canonical_epoch=19 -- best-validation and the canonical FINAL_STEP_1350 checkpoint are DIFFERENT checkpoints (different export_path, different sha256) for this real, already-trained seed. Had M9.6 used best-validation as authoritative, its own frozen decision would rest on a materially earlier, less-exposed checkpoint for that seed.

corrected_m9_8_checkpoint_policy.ARM_S: Reuse M9.6's own SHA-verified canonical checkpoint: read m9-6-training-runs/ARM_B_M9_6-seed{seed}.json's `canonical_export_path`/`canonical_export_sha256` (NOT `best_validation_export_path`/`best_validation_export_sha256`), recompute the SHA-256 of the file at `canonical_export_path` and compare against `canonical_export_sha256`; on match, load it as ARM_S's model for that seed. On mismatch or physical absence, follow the SAME REUSED_M9_6_CHECKPOINT / REGENERATED_NOT_ORIGINAL_M9_6_CHECKPOINT transparency procedure m9-7-m9-8-preregistration.json already specifies -- unchanged except that 'M9.6's own trained checkpoints' now unambiguously means the canonical FINAL_STEP_1350 export.
corrected_m9_8_checkpoint_policy.ARM_M: Train exactly 1350 optimizer steps (unchanged from M9.7), then apply M9.6's OWN Section-14 procedure verbatim: reload the LAST periodic checkpoint (epoch 20 / global_step 1350, guaranteed to exist since early_stopping_patience=0 per the frozen recipe) into a FRESH model instance and export it separately as the canonical, promotion-authoritative checkpoint (`model-export-final-step.safetensors`, `canonical_checkpoint_policy='FINAL_STEP_1350'`, `canonical_global_step=1350`, `canonical_epoch=19`). This canonical export -- not the best-validation export `Trainer.fit()` writes along the way -- is ARM_M's authoritative M9.8 checkpoint.
corrected_m9_8_checkpoint_policy.best_validation_checkpoints: MAY still be saved and reported for both arms (M9.6's own scripts already do this via `best_validation_export_path`/`best_validation_export_sha256`/`best_epoch`) for diagnostic/convergence-monitoring purposes only. They MUST NOT be loaded for, or in any way determine, the M9.8 Section-12 guardrail evaluation, the paired-bootstrap primary-endpoint comparison, or any A-E promotion decision. Any M9.8 result artifact that reports a best-validation-checkpoint number MUST label it diagnostic-only and keep it structurally separate from the canonical FINAL_STEP_1350 numbers the promotion decision actually uses -- mirroring M9.6's own record-keeping convention exactly (both fields present, only one authoritative).
